title: Zaha Hadid
objective: After this level you can describe Hadid's flowing buildings.
summary: Long called a paper architect, Zaha Hadid designed through painting, built the angular Vitra Fire Station in 1993, and later folded whole plazas into buildings. In 2004 she won the Pritzker Prize.

cards.headline: For years, Zaha Hadid was labeled a paper architect.
cards.body: She kept winning competitions, starting with The Peak, a leisure club in Hong Kong, in 1983. But her winning designs often went unbuilt. In 2004 she became the first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize. How do you get from paper to that?

cards.headline: Designing with paint
cards.body: Hadid was born in Baghdad in 1950, studied mathematics in Beirut, then trained as an architect in London. Especially early on, painting and drawing were how she investigated a design. Her work drew on Kazimir Malevich and the Suprematist painters, and it shared their sense of fragmentation, instability and movement. Her paintings weren't illustrations of buildings. They were how she found them.

cards.fact: Her first major building was a fire station.
cards.context: The Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein, Germany, was finished in 1993: a series of sharply angled, tilted planes of exposed concrete. Her office called it "movement frozen", a building tense and alert, ready to explode into action when the alarm rang. It no longer houses fire engines; it's used for exhibitions and events.

mascot.line: Even standing still, it looks like it's about to leave. Which, for a fire station, is the job.

cards.headline: From shards to waves
cards.body: Her later buildings flow. Her office's Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, completed in 2012, seems to rise out of its plaza as if the ground itself had been lifted, curved and folded. Floor, wall, ceiling and roof blur into one surface. The sharp shards of the fire station had become long, continuous waves.

questions.prompt: Why was Zaha Hadid once labeled a 'paper architect'?

options.label: She designed buildings made of paper
options.rationale: The label was about designs that stayed on paper.

options.label: She worked only as a magazine critic
Her winning designs often went unbuilt

questions.prompt: What did Hadid's office mean by calling the Vitra Fire Station 'movement frozen'?

options.label: It was built in winter
options.rationale: The phrase is about its form.

options.label: Its walls slide open like doors
options.rationale: It's about the angled planes expressing tension.

options.label: Its angled planes look tense, ready to burst into action
It was cooled to protect the fire engines
options.rationale: The phrase describes its sense of motion.

questions.explanation: Its sharply angled planes express tension, a building alert and ready to explode into action when the alarm rings.
